findings.text: Provides removal of a filesystem name relative to a directory descriptor and kernel filename object, resolving the parent and final component, requiring a normal last element, holding a write reference on the mount, performing the child removal under a directory operation context, and retrying with revalidation when a stale handle is reported.

Deletes a non-directory entry from a parent inode after validating deletability, requiring a filesystem unlink operation, excluding swap and locally mounted targets, invoking security and delegation handling, detaching mounts on success, and emitting link count or deletion notifications.

Authorizes deletion of a child dentry by checking existence, identity mapping validity, parent write and execute permission, append and immutable protections, sticky directory rules, directory versus non-directory expectations, liveness of the parent, and NFS silly rename state.
Opens a user pathname string with supplied flags and mode by converting the string to a kernel filename object and delegating to the common name based open path at the current working directory.
Opens a kernel filename object by normalizing caller flags and mode into an intermediate description and then into kernel open intents and lookup controls before invoking the file open worker.
Releases a directory operation handle by unlocking the parent inode and dropping the dentry reference when the handle does not represent a lookup failure.

Reports whether a dentry serves as a mountpoint in the current mount namespace by first testing the dentry mount flag and then scanning the namespace mount collection for a matching mountpoint under shared namespace protection.

Resolves a parent directory and final name from a directory descriptor and filename by initializing lookup state, walking the path, completing traversal, returning the parent path while clearing walker state, and retrying without optimistic lookup or with revalidation on specific transient failures while auditing the parent.

Converts caller open flags and mode into kernel open state, masking to valid bits, restricting path-only opens to a narrow subset, clearing mode unless creation was requested, validating resolve controls, and deriving access mode plus lookup intent and scoping flags.

Implements piped core handling by guarding against recursive invocation and pipe overload, building helper arguments from stored offsets, launching a user helper and requiring its output file, plus file based dumping by snapshotting address ranges, bracketing the format writer with write guards, padding skipped bytes, and releasing the snapshot.

Collects dumpable address ranges by counting mappable areas plus an optional gate area, recording boundaries and flags with per-range dump sizes and file references, resolving deferred header checks after releasing the address lock, accumulating total dump bytes, and optionally ordering entries by size.

Unlink requires a normal trailing component; non-normal endings are rejected with a directory error, and names with an embedded separator after the final element are rejected as directory or non-directory errors depending on whether the target is a directory.

On successful removal the target is marked non-mountable and detached from mount tables; NFS silly renamed entries generate only an unlink notification while other successes generate link count and delete notifications with appropriate reference handling.

Deletion fails when the victim is negative, when mapped identity is invalid, when the parent lacks write or execute rights, when append or immutable or swap protections apply, when sticky rules deny, when directory expectations mismatch, when the parent is dead, or when the victim carries an NFS renamed marker.

Parent lookup first attempts an optimistic walk, falls back to a blocking walk on optimistic failure, and revalidates on stale handles; success copies the final name and type and audits the parent, and stale errors without a revalidation flag trigger an outer retry.

Open construction rejects unknown flag bits, unknown resolve bits, conflicting scoping modes, directory combined with creation, tmpfile without directory or without write access, directory combined with regular-file-only request, path-only combined with disallowed bits, and cached resolve combined with truncate or creation.

Path-only opens are limited to a small flag subset, clear general access rights, and suppress the open lookup intent, while other opens carry an open intent extended with create and exclusive markers when requested.

A user visible regular-file-only request expressed in upper flag bits is translated to an internal lower-bit carrier so it survives narrowing to the kernel flag field and later file flag propagation, with removal before user visibility.

Piped dumping aborts when the resource limit indicates recursion, upgrades the limit to unlimited otherwise, tracks concurrent pipe count against a configurable ceiling, and treats allocation failure or helper launch failure as a skipped dump.

Range dump size is full for always-dump areas including gate and named or architecture markers, zero for non-dumpable or device mappings, and otherwise gated by DAX, huge page, shared versus private, anonymous, and mapped filters with unlinked shared files treated as anonymous.

A readable file mapping at zero offset with header filtering may contribute a single page to help identification when executable permission is present, otherwise a placeholder is recorded during locked collection and later resolved by inspecting user bytes for header magic.
A directory operation holds the parent inode lock from setup until explicit release, which unlocks the parent and drops the child reference.
Unlink mutation holds the target inode lock across swap and mountpoint checks, security authorization, delegation breaks, and the filesystem removal operation.
Marking a dentry as non-mountable is performed under the dentry spin lock.
Testing for a local mountpoint holds shared namespace protection while iterating the mount collection in the current namespace.

Snapshot collection acquires the address space write lock in killable mode, releases it after copying range descriptors and taking file references, and only then performs user memory inspection and accounting.

Unlink proceeds through parent resolution, mount write hold, child lookup, authorization, removal, delegation wait with inner retry of the child lookup, write release, path release, and outer revalidation retry on stale results.

Open flag processing moves from legacy flag normalization and sync expansion through mode validation, conflict checks, access derivation with truncate and append augmentation, intent selection, and resolve-driven lookup scoping.

File dumping checks for interruption, captures the address snapshot, brackets the format specific writer between file write guards, emits a padding byte when trailing skip remains, and frees per-range references.
Address iteration yields successive mappable areas in order and then yields the gate area at most once, terminating when both sources are exhausted or when the gate was already returned.
Attempts to remove swap files, local mountpoints, root directories, dead parents, or NFS renamed entries fail rather than mutating namespace state.
Deletion with unmapped or invalid ownership identities fails with an overflow style error before permission checks complete.
A piped dump with no helper output file after successful helper execution is reported as disabled and treated as no dump.
Unlink notification assumes a positive dentry and warns when presented with a negative entry instead of emitting an event.

Error facts include EISDIR for directory mismatch, ENOTDIR for slashed non-directory, ENOENT for missing or dead targets, EPERM for protection or missing operation, EBUSY for mountpoint or root, EOVERFLOW for invalid identity, EINVAL for bad open or resolve arguments, EAGAIN for cached create, ESTALE for stale handles, and ECHILD for optimistic retry.

Flag facts include O_PATH with its narrow allowed subset, O_CREAT and __O_TMPFILE as creation markers, O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW and O_EMPTYPATH and O_TRUNC and O_APPEND as behavior modifiers, LOOKUP_DIRECTORY and LOOKUP_FOLLOW and LOOKUP_EMPTY and LOOKUP_NO_XDEV and LOOKUP_NO_SYMLINKS and LOOKUP_BENEATH and LOOKUP_IN_ROOT and LOOKUP_CACHED and LOOKUP_REVAL and LOOKUP_RCU as lookup controls, MAY_WRITE and MAY_EXEC and MAY_APPEND as access rights, and masking to all permission bits.

Cache and notification facts include a cant-mount dentry marker set under lock, an attribute notification for link count changes, and delete notifications that drop the dentry while holding an inode reference.

Open handling uses an intermediate user oriented descriptor carrying flags and mode and resolve controls and a kernel oriented descriptor carrying normalized mode and narrowed flags plus derived access rights and lookup intent and scoping state.

Snapshot entries record start and end addresses, mapping flags, computed dump length, file offset, and an optional referenced file object, with a count and total byte accumulator held alongside the array.
Provides a lexical scope construct built on a class based override helper for initial filesystem context.
Access mode derivation maps the open access selector to a combination of read and write permission requirements.
